# OSH Code 2020 Transition Briefing — Factory (Delhi / Central)

**Prepared for:** the Occupier / client  
**Prepared by:** the reviewing competent person (HSE Advisory)  
**Date:** 5 July 2026  
**State / jurisdiction:** Delhi / Central (DL) — Factory (Factories Act, 1948)  
**Purpose:** What to file now, and how the OSH Code 2020 changes filing obligations for this establishment

---

## What to File Now

**File Form 21.** This is the annual return prescribed under the Delhi / Central pattern of the Factories Act 1948 and its cognate rules. It remains the only valid, regulator-accepted annual return for Delhi factories as at 5 July 2026.

| Detail | Value |
|---|---|
| Form | **Form 21** (Delhi / Central pattern) |
| Obligation | Annual return — Factories Act 1948 |
| Due | On or before **1 February** following the close of the calendar year to which the return relates |
| Portal | State / Central portal — verify the current e-filing mechanism with the Delhi Chief Inspector of Factories before submission |
| Authority | Inspector of Factories, Delhi |

*Source: KB-REG-IN-STATEFORMS (DL row, factories-act, annual-return). Verified 17 June 2026.*

---

## Direction of Travel — India's Four Labour Codes

India is consolidating 44 central labour laws into four codes. All four codes received Presidential assent; commencement is state-by-state and largely pending.

| Code | Key laws absorbed | Relevance to this factory |
|---|---|---|
| Code on Wages, 2019 | Minimum Wages Act, Payment of Wages Act, Payment of Bonus Act, Equal Remuneration Act | Wage-related registers and returns |
| Industrial Relations Code, 2020 | Trade Unions Act, Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, Industrial Disputes Act | Standing orders, dispute procedures |
| Code on Social Security, 2020 | EPF Act, ESI Act, Maternity Benefit Act, Gratuity Act, + others | Social security contributions and returns |
| **Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (OSH Code — Act 37 of 2020)** | **Factories Act 1948, BOCW Act 1996, Mines Act 1952 + 10 others (13 laws total)** | **Annual return, registration, accident notice, Safety Officer** |

The OSH Code is the instrument that absorbs the Factories Act. Its direction of travel — single registration, single consolidated annual return, unified portal — is the material change for this establishment.

---

## What the OSH Code Changes for Factories

Four headline changes when the OSH Code commences in a state:

**1. Single registration.** The per-law factory licence issued by the Inspector of Factories collapses into one consolidated establishment registration covering all applicable laws.

**2. Single consolidated annual return.** Multiple per-law periodic returns are replaced by one unified annual return filed against a single consolidated form.

**3. Factory threshold raised.** The Factories Act triggers at 10 workers (manufacturing process with power) or 20 workers (without power). The OSH Code raises these thresholds to **20 workers (with power) / 40 workers (without power)**. Establishments that fall below the new threshold may exit the factory regime; those currently marginal should audit headcount against both sets of thresholds.

**4. Safety Officer threshold tightened.** Under the Factories Act the Safety Officer appointment is mandatory at 1,000 workers. The OSH Code proposes to lower this to **500 workers** (or **250 workers** in hazardous processes) — a more onerous duty, not a relaxation.

## Legacy → Consolidated Mapping Table

| Obligation | Legacy (Factories Act — Delhi, live today) | OSH-Code consolidation (direction of travel) | Live in Delhi (DL)? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Annual return | **Form 21**, by ~1 February, to Inspector of Factories | Single consolidated annual return | **[GAP] — DL OSH Rules not notified** |
| Registration / licence | Factory licence, Inspector of Factories | Single consolidated establishment registration | **[GAP] — DL OSH Rules not notified** |
| Accident notice | Per Factories Act / Delhi state rules | Accident-notice duty expressly retained in OSH Code | Continue filing legacy notice (savings clause) |
| Filing portal | State / Central portal (verify locally) | Shram Suvidha — unified filing portal (direction only) | Partial implementation — verify locally |
| Safety Officer | Mandatory at 1,000 workers | Mandatory at 500 / 250 workers (hazardous) | **[GAP] — DL OSH Rules not notified** |

## Per-State Notification Status

The OSH Code commences on a state-by-state basis as each state notifies its OSH Rules. As at 5 July 2026:

| State | OSH Rules notified? | Practical position |
|---|---|---|
| **Gujarat (GJ)** | **Yes — notified** | GJ establishments should verify with local authority whether consolidated obligations have replaced legacy filings and whether the consolidated form is live |
| **Arunachal Pradesh (AR)** | **Yes — notified** | Same — verify locally before relying on consolidated form |
| **Delhi / Central (DL)** | **No — OSH Rules not notified** | Legacy Form 21 is the only valid annual return; consolidated form is **[GAP]** |
| All other states | Largely pending | Legacy filings under respective state rules remain valid and required |

> **Staleness caution:** State notification status is a rapidly-changing regulatory fact. This briefing reflects the position as at 5 July 2026 and carries a 90-day review horizon. Verify current commencement status before acting or before the next filing cycle.

---

## Caution — Do Not File an Unnotified Form

Delhi has not notified its OSH Rules. No consolidated annual-return form has been prescribed for Delhi factories under the OSH Code. **Do not file a consolidated OSH-Code form that the state has not notified.** Such a filing would have no legal effect and would leave the legacy Form 21 obligation unsatisfied — creating a compliance gap rather than resolving one.

Every reference to the Delhi consolidated form in this briefing is marked **[GAP]** for this reason. Treat each [GAP] as a standing action item: monitor the Delhi Gazette for OSH Rules notification and update this filing map when notification occurs.

---

## Savings Clause

The OSH Code 2020 (Section 143) contains a savings clause: until a provision is commenced and the relevant state notifies its OSH Rules, all obligations under the repealed Acts remain in full force. There is no gap in the filing obligation during the transition. Form 21 is valid, required, and enforceable for Delhi factories today.

---

## Recommended Actions

| # | Action | Owner | Timing |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | File **Form 21** with the Delhi Inspector of Factories for the applicable return period | the Occupier | On or before 1 February following the return year |
| 2 | Verify the current e-filing portal / submission mechanism with the Delhi Chief Inspector of Factories | the Occupier | Before the next filing cycle |
| 3 | Audit worker headcount against both sets of factory thresholds — current (10/20) and OSH-Code (20/40) — to assess whether establishment status changes on commencement | the reviewing competent person | Within 30 days |
| 4 | Monitor Delhi Gazette for OSH Rules notification; update this mapping and transition the filing obligation to the consolidated form only when notified | the reviewing competent person | Ongoing — review at 90-day intervals |
| 5 | Assess Safety Officer appointment obligation against the proposed OSH-Code threshold (500 / 250 hazardous workers) and plan for the tightened duty | the reviewing competent person | When DL OSH Rules notified |
